diagnostics.message: The AWS Config delivery channel in ap-northeast-1 delivers configuration snapshots to the audit log S3 bucket, but it has no dependency on aws_s3_bucket_policy.audit_log. The bucket policy that grants config.amazonaws.com s3:PutObject is only connected through the bucket resource itself (via the local.audit_log_bucket_id local), so Terraform creates the delivery channel in parallel with — and often after — the policy is applied, causing InsufficientDeliveryPolicyException / failed snapshot delivery. CloudTrail is protected from this exact race via cloudtrail_depends_on = [aws_s3_bucket_policy.audit_log]; add the same ordering (e.g. depends_on = [aws_s3_bucket_policy.audit_log]) here.

The configuration recorder in ap-northeast-1 is started (is_enabled = true) without any ordering against aws_iam_role_policy.recorder_publish_policy, which grants the recorder role s3:PutObject on the audit log bucket and sns:Publish on the config SNS topics. The role policy is created in parallel with the config-baseline modules, so recording can start before the role has permission to deliver. The aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.recorder_read_policy (AWS_ConfigRole) has the same gap. Add depends_on for the recorder role policy/attachment.

When vpc_flow_logs_destination_type is "s3", the default-VPC flow logs in ap-northeast-1 deliver to the audit log bucket, but this module has no ordering against aws_s3_bucket_policy.audit_log — the resource that grants delivery.logs.amazonaws.com s3:PutObject on that bucket. The module only references the bucket itself (through the flow_logs_s3_arn local), so flow logs can be created before the policy is applied and log delivery will fail until it lands. Add depends_on = [aws_s3_bucket_policy.audit_log].
